2 marks: municipal by-law = macro / external legal-political environment; 2 marks: late-order issue = internal operations (accept micro only if linked to controllable workflow).

Award up to 4 linked pairs: compliance cost/capital for grease traps; inspection time or temporary disruption; changed process and record keeping; customer confidence if compliant. One mark for each relevant effect and one for its explanation/application.

Up to 4 marks per response: select order tracking/capacity scheduling or customer recovery/communication; explain how it reduces delay or repairs trust. Credit other feasible responses tied to the complaint.

Up to 8: employee voice reveals shift constraints; early consultation builds buy-in; identifies lawful/fair options; reduces conflict and implementation risk. Award a relevant point and its explanation for each strand; consultation does not replace legal duties.

Up to 12: demand/capacity evidence; capital and working-capital affordability given tight cash flow; supplier and staffing readiness; staged pilot/lease alternative; risk of delay versus growth benefit; explicit justified recommendation. Up to 2 marks per developed consideration.
2 marks: threat is an external condition with adverse effect; 2 marks: opportunity is an external condition with potential benefit. Internal strengths/weaknesses are not threats/opportunities.

Award 1 mark for each force correctly identified and 1 for explaining its effect: rivalry, new entrants, substitutes, buyer power, supplier power. Up to 8; market application strengthens the explanation.

Any four distinct links (2 each): fair recruitment/equal opportunity; lawful employment terms/hours; employee relations/collective processes; workplace health and safety; privacy/data handling. Name a relevant duty and show its HR consequence.

Up to 5 per pressure: online competitor response (differentiate, improve digital convenience, retain customers, or focused pricing) and transport cost response (consolidate deliveries, review sourcing/location, load-plan or transparent pricing); explain effect and trade-off for each.

Benefits: scans political, economic, social, technological, legal and environmental context; structures assumptions; spots external change. Limits: broad/static, data quality, uncertain timing, cannot replace competitor/customer/financial analysis. Award balanced evaluation and justified use.
Plan a standard; do the process; check results against the standard; act to correct and improve. One mark each in a coherent cycle.
Up to 4 paired explanations: induction clarifies role/rules/process; skills development builds competence; fewer errors/waste; confidence/safety/service improves.
Any four, 2 marks each when explained: total cost; quality/specification; reliability/lead time; capacity/continuity; compliance/ethical sourcing; location/logistics; support/payment terms.

Up to 10: define output/quality standard; measure by shift using consistent records; compare actual to target; identify causes (staffing, equipment, inputs); agree corrective action; train/support; assign owner/date; remeasure and document. Award feasible measurable steps.

Up to 10 balanced application: productivity through workflow and standards; wellbeing through safe staffing, breaks and voice; customer service through reliable quality and clear recovery; monitor trade-offs with measures; recommend a practical balance.

2 marks: using competitor photos risks copyright / intellectual-property infringement; 2 marks: misleading or unsubstantiated crowdfunding claims can damage trust or create legal/reputational exposure. Accept only distinct risks.

Up to 4 paired comparisons: co-operative member ownership/participation versus company shareholding/directors; governance/decision process; ability to raise equity; liability/continuity subject to law and governing documents. Avoid unqualified liability claims.

Up to 4 per method: prototype trials with target users and structured feedback; small preorder/deposit test with transparent terms; landing-page/price test; interviews/survey with defined sample. Explain evidence produced; do not infer demand.

Up to 8: acknowledge/log complaint; test failure mode; check warranty/consumer obligations; repair/replace/refund where appropriate; communicate timing; improve design/quality control; monitor recurrence. Award response plus reason/application.

Up to 12: credit can preserve cash for operations; compare financing cost and repayment timing with cash forecast; identify security/asset-loss exposure; check covenants and supplier dependency; negotiate capped pilot/terms; conditional recommendation on affordability/security review.
Any four: executive/venture summary; market/customer analysis; marketing and sales plan; operations; management/team; financial forecasts/funding; risks and milestones. One mark per distinct element.

Up to 8: define fixed costs, selling price and variable cost; calculate contribution; derive break-even volume (fixed cost ÷ contribution per unit); compare with realistic demand/capacity; state assumptions and margin-of-safety implication.

Any four appropriate sources with stage/use fit (2 each): founder capital/bootstrapping; retained earnings; loan/overdraft; grant/prize; equity investor; supplier credit; crowdfunding with transparent terms. Explain one benefit or constraint each.

Up to 10 comparative analysis: sole proprietor has simpler control but owner bears business risk and continuity depends on owner; private company has separate legal personality/continuity and can issue shares subject to law, but more governance/filing and shared control. Apply liability/control/continuity; avoid unqualified legal advice.

Benefits: identifies needs, willingness to pay, competitors and channel; supports pricing/forecast/testing. Limits: sample/bias, stale data, stated intent differs from purchase, cost/time and residual uncertainty. Conclude how to combine research with a small real test.
Any four: honesty; fairness/respect; accountability; transparency; confidentiality/privacy; integrity; avoiding harm/conflicts. One mark per applicable distinct principle.

CSR is planned, sustained responsibility integrated into decisions and impacts; a once-off donation is limited and may not change business practices. Award for distinction, stakeholder/environment examples and explanation.

Any four actions, 2 each when explained: fair accessible recruitment; consistent criteria/pay; accommodation/accessibility; anti-harassment reporting; diverse voice in decisions; training and accountable review of outcomes.

Up to 10: private benefit can bias a decision; unfair supplier/employee treatment harms stakeholders; disclose interests; recuse conflicted decision-maker; independent review/dual approval; maintain records and enforce policy. Link harm to control.

Up to 10 balanced response: economic viability and lifecycle cost; social effects on workers/community; environmental resource/emissions/waste effects; measurable targets and monitoring; trade-offs and feasible staged recommendation.
